Hemdean Road.road: Two-way distributor road with white centre line, bus route with bus stops, double yellow lines in places and side-street give-way junctions; fairly wide at the north end with grass verges.
Hemdean Road.note: Long road: the south end is Victorian/Edwardian red brick terraces with slate roofs, bays and low brick front walls (many paved for parking), with Edwardian semis having white-rendered gables; the north end becomes interwar semis with red brick ground floors, white render or pebbledash upstairs, brown tile roofs and hedges.

Surley Row.road: Winding two-way road, partly no centre line, a 20 mph roundel at one point and 30 mph signs elsewhere; grass verges and footpath cut-throughs; narrow and leafy at the south end with high old brick walls.
Surley Row.note: Very leafy: many views are mostly trees, hedges and old high brick garden walls. Older white-rendered Georgian/Victorian houses near the south end, then 1960s-80s and modern detached houses in brown/orange brick, plus some postwar semis on open lawns.

Blenheim Road.road: Residential street, no centre line, cars parked along the kerbs, fairly narrow; footways both sides, gentle curves.
Blenheim Road.note: Late Victorian/Edwardian villas and semis: red brick with buff or white dressings, several silver-grey Reading brick fronts with red-brick quoins, white bay windows and slate roofs; some Edwardian semis with mock-Tudor gables. A few 1970s-80s infill detached houses in orange brick. Low brick walls and hedges in front.

Balmore Drive.note: Google has no Street View imagery along Balmore Drive; the junction views snapped onto Peppard Road and show that road instead.

Rotherfield Way.road: Wide-ish residential road, no centre line, grass verges, give-way markings at junctions; some kerbside parking.
Rotherfield Way.note: Southern end has 1930s semis and detached houses with red brick ground floors and white-rendered upper floors under red/brown tile hipped roofs; further north 1960s-70s detached houses and chalet bungalows in buff/orange brick with white boarding, behind hedges and big trees.

Picton Way.road: Quiet estate cul-de-sac, no centre line, double yellow lines at the entrance, rounded kerbs and a turning head; no parking bays.
Picton Way.note: 1970s-80s executive estate of detached houses in orange-brown brick with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages and some tile-hung or boarded panels, set behind open-plan lawns and block-paved drives among mature trees.

Balmore Park.road: Curving estate road with rounded kerbs, no centre line or markings apart from the street name painted at the junction; wide grass verges; no parking bays.
Balmore Park.note: 1980s-90s estate of detached houses and a few semis in red and orange-brown brick under brown or dark plain-tile roofs, some with white-rendered first floors, porch canopies and integral garages; open-plan lawns and set in mature woodland.

Stuart Close.road: Narrow-ish estate close with no centre line, wide grass verges and a grassed island at the entrance junction; turning circle at the end; cars parked on drives and kerbside.
Stuart Close.note: Postwar semis in red brick, many with cream/buff rendered upper floors, under hipped brown or dark tile roofs, plus a few bungalows; fronts are a mix of hedges, low brick walls, fences and paved drives, with grass verges.

Scott Close.road: Narrow estate cul-de-sac with no markings, block-paved parking spaces and communal parking courts; open grass between the terraces and the road.
Scott Close.note: 1970s estate of plain two-storey terraces in orange-brown and buff brick with shallow brown concrete-tile roofs and flat porch canopies, plus a few bungalows; open-plan lawns, paths and timber fences, backing onto woodland.

Buckingham Drive.road: Wide estate spine road with a white centre line and very wide grass verges with young trees, separate service roads/parking laybys in front of the houses; give-way markings at junctions.
Buckingham Drive.note: Postwar council-built estate: semis and short terraces in red brick, many with cream-rendered or panelled upper floors (one terrace has green-painted upper panels), hipped brown tile roofs, and three-storey brown-brick flat blocks set back behind big greens. Two of the three panoramas date from 2012.

Queen Street.road: Narrow residential street with no centre line or markings; on-street parking on one side; steep wooded bank behind at the west end.
Queen Street.note: Victorian two-storey red-brick terraces with slate roofs, small bays and low brick front walls, a white-rendered end house and a white-rendered Victorian cottage; at the western end some 1980s-2000s red-brick semis with gravel parking.

Evesham Road.road: Wide estate road with dashed centre line in places, give-way markings at the junctions with Grove Road and Knights Way, broad grass verges and greens set back from the carriageway.
Evesham Road.note: Late-1940s/50s semis with red brick ground floors and pebbledash or cream render above, hipped brown/dark tile roofs and chimneys, set back behind privet hedges, low fences and wide grass greens with mature trees.

Priest Hill.road: Residential road climbing a hill, faint centre line in places, give-way markings at side junctions, kerbside parking; mature street trees at the upper end.
Priest Hill.note: Edwardian red-brick detached houses and semis with gables, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor timbering or white-rendered upper storeys, bay windows and dark plain-tile or slate roofs; Victorian red-brick terraces near the bottom; low brick walls and hedges, many front gardens paved for parking.

Grove Hill.road: Narrow lane-like road on a hill with no centre line, a narrow footway on one side only, grass verges, thick hedges and trees right up to the carriageway.
Grove Hill.note: Most views are tall hedges and trees; the houses glimpsed are detached chalet bungalows and 1960s-70s houses with white render and dormers or orange/red brick, under brown or dark tile roofs, plus a few older red-brick houses.

Berrylands Road.road: Quiet residential road with no centre line, yellow lines at junction corners, grass verges with trees on part; low-traffic loop.
Berrylands Road.note: 1950s semis in red and orange-red brick with hipped or gabled brown/dark tile roofs and side garages, plus several white-rendered semis and a few detached houses; fronts of low brick walls, close-board fences and hedges, many paved drives.

Cedarwood Crescent.road: Curving estate cul-de-sac, no centre line or markings, rounded kerbs, block-paved drives; quiet.
Cedarwood Crescent.note: 1980s estate of red-brick detached and link-detached houses and a few bungalows with dark brown concrete plain-tile roofs, integral garages and lean-to porch roofs; open-plan lawns mixed with shrubs, hedges and some low brick walls, with mature conifers and trees.

St Anne's Road.road: Two-way road with white centre line, double yellow lines on long stretches, give-way markings at junctions; slopes up the hill; some kerbside parking.
St Anne's Road.note: Large late-Victorian and Edwardian villas and semis in red brick, some silver-grey Reading brick with red-brick dressings and some painted white, with bays, gables (several with mock-Tudor timbering) and slate or dark tile roofs; low brick walls, hedges and paved drives.

Chaucer Close.road: Short estate cul-de-sac with no markings, a tarmac parking court and a row of flat-roofed white-door lock-up garages; small grass verges.
Chaucer Close.note: 1970s estate of plain two-storey terraces and end houses in orange-brown brick with brown or grey concrete tile roofs, mostly seen gable-end on behind a parking court and a block of lock-up garages.

Bridge Street.road: Busy A-road (A4155) through the centre with white centre line and lane markings, pedestrian crossings and bollards, bus stops, wide paved footways; heavy traffic near Caversham Bridge.
Bridge Street.shops: Almost the whole frontage is shops, pubs and offices: ground-floor shopfronts with large plate glass and dark grey, navy, blue or black painted fascias with white lettering, a few hanging baskets; mostly one or two storeys of flats/offices above in red brick, grey Reading brick or white render with bay or sash windows; a pub painted blue-grey with a tiled roof, a red-brick Victorian gabled commercial block, and a single-storey tyre/brake garage forecourt with a red-and-white fascia.
Bridge Street.note: Caversham's main shopping street: two- and three-storey Victorian and Edwardian buildings built up to the pavement, mixed red brick, grey brick and painted render, with continuous shopfronts and a busy main road.

Derby Road.note: Google has no Street View imagery at either survey point on Derby Road ('No Street View imagery available here').

Brill Close.road: Narrow sloping cul-de-sac with no markings apart from the street name, no footway on one side where hedges and fences line the road; block-paved drives.
Brill Close.note: Mix of 1960s-70s bungalows and chalet bungalows in orange brick with white boarding, and 1980s-90s red-brick detached houses with dark brown tile roofs, tile-hung bays and integral garages; open-plan fronts and paved drives, hedges and fences on the lower section.

The Ridgeway.road: Residential estate road with no centre line, yellow lines at corners, wide grass verges with trees and a grassed triangle at a junction.
The Ridgeway.note: 1960s semis in red brick with white-painted boarded or rendered panels on the upper floor, integral garages and brown/dark tile roofs, set behind open lawns and drives; wide grass verges and mature trees, a wooded bank at one end.

Eliot Close.road: Narrow estate road with no markings, kerbside parking, grass verge and footpath through a green; woodland edge.
Eliot Close.note: Only one useful view: 1960s-70s two-storey terraces in red-brown brick with white panels under the windows, shallow brown-tile roofs, concrete-panel and close-board fences and small front gardens; the other view is a grassy green and trees.

Ellesmere Close.note: Google has no Street View imagery at either survey point on Ellesmere Close ('No Street View imagery available here').

Hemdean Rise.road: Narrow sloping residential street, dashed centre line in parts, give-way at junctions, cars parked along both kerbs.
Hemdean Rise.note: Late-Victorian/Edwardian red-brick terraces with front gables, two-storey bays, buff/red brick string courses and slate roofs, one terrace in grey Reading brick with red dressings; small front gardens behind low brick walls.
